body.name: Worked exact certificate for the rational witness
body.construction:
The exact certificate \(\mathcal C^\star\) is the following finite transcript for the rational input in \(P^\star\).  Put
\[
W(t)=\frac{16t}{1+15t},\qquad
d_\vartheta(z)=\frac{\vartheta z}{1+(\vartheta-1)z}-z,
\]
and, for \(\vartheta\in\{1/36,36\}\), define
\[
J_\vartheta(t)=\frac{29}{100}
+\frac{W(t)-t}{2}\{d_\vartheta(z_1)+d_\vartheta(z_0)\},
\]
where the legal roots \(z_1,z_0\in(0,1)\) solve the following primitive integer polynomials:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
F_{1,-}=3500tz_1^2-3500tz_1-3500z_1^2+5455z_1-1908,
&F_{0,-}=875tz_0^2+2650tz_0-3240t-875z_0^2+1110z_0-216,\\
F_{1,+}=-3500tz_1^2+3500tz_1+3500z_1^2-1755z_1-53,
&F_{0,+}=-875tz_0^2+11225tz_0-90t+875z_0^2-185z_0-6.
\end{array}
\tag{C1}
\]
Here the minus and plus signs denote \(\vartheta=1/36\) and \(\vartheta=36\), respectively.  Let \(S_\pm\) be the primitive numerator, with positive leading-coefficient convention, of
\[
\frac{\partial J_\vartheta}{\partial t}
\frac{\partial F_{1,\pm}}{\partial z_1}
\frac{\partial F_{0,\pm}}{\partial z_0}
-\frac{\partial J_\vartheta}{\partial z_1}
\frac{\partial F_{1,\pm}}{\partial t}
\frac{\partial F_{0,\pm}}{\partial z_0}
-\frac{\partial J_\vartheta}{\partial z_0}
\frac{\partial F_{0,\pm}}{\partial t}
\frac{\partial F_{1,\pm}}{\partial z_1}.
\tag{C2}
\]
Equations (C1)--(C2) are the full defining stationary systems; no derivative or denominator is implicit.  After saturation by \(t(1-t)(1+15t)\), the two tilt denominators, and the two derivatives \(\partial F_{a,\pm}/\partial z_a\), the square-free \(t\)-factors of
\(\operatorname{Res}_{z_0}(F_{0,\pm},\operatorname{Res}_{z_1}(F_{1,\pm},S_\pm))\)
are
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_-(t)={}&4404233927002616960449218750000000000t^{16}
-8155898270853641527324218750000000000t^{15}\\
&+8359990543068833524025214843750000000t^{14}

-233660036575247382485832406410t\\
&+11933213589796668025115770443,
\end{aligned}
\tag{C3}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_+(t)={}&6602797178337116825836523437500000000000t^{16}

&+16287023439341598675579810131.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C4}
\]
For a square-free integer polynomial \(g\), its Sturm chain in this transcript means the deterministic rational-remainder chain \(s_0=g\), \(s_1=g'\), and \(s_{j+1}=-\operatorname{rem}(s_{j-1},s_j)\), with no sign renormalization.  The signs and variation counts are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
g&\text{rational argument}&(\operatorname{sgn}s_0,\ldots,\operatorname{sgn}s_{16});\ V\\ \hline
g_-&0&+--++++--++-+++-+;\ 8\\
g_-&1&+++--++++--++-+++;\ 6\\
g_-&251392284/10^9&+--+++-----+-+-++;\ 8\\
g_-&251392285/10^9&---+++-----+-+-++;\ 7\\
g_-&301842750/10^9&-++---+++++-+--++;\ 7\\
g_-&301842751/10^9&+++---+++++-+--++;\ 6\\ \hline
g_+&0&+--+----+++-+--++;\ 8\\
g_+&1&++---+++----++--+;\ 6\\
g_+&157087585/10^9&+--++---+++-++--+;\ 8\\
g_+&157087586/10^9&---++---+++-++--+;\ 7\\
g_+&242967344/10^9&-++--+++++--++--+;\ 7\\
g_+&242967345/10^9&+++--+++++--++--+;\ 6.
\end{array}
\tag{C5}
\]
Thus each polynomial has exactly two roots in \((0,1)\), one in each displayed interval.  Rational interval Newton evaluation of the original three-equation systems gives the complete legal reverse-arc candidate table
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c}
\vartheta&t&W(t)&z_1&z_0&J_\vartheta\\ \hline
1/36&[251392284,251392285]&[843088267,843088268]&[688551450,688551451]&[841040182,841040183]&[-107500302,-107500301]\\
1/36&[301842750,301842751]&[873697076,873697077]&[729071357,729071358]&[863832034,863832035]&[-102730735,-102730734]\\
36&[157087585,157087586]&[748857684,748857685]&[448563283,448563284]&[12683976,12683977]&[533207555,533207556]\\
36&[242967344,242967345]&[837004844,837004845]&[392390615,392390616]&[10930193,10930194]&[539509967,539509968].
\end{array}
\tag{C6}
\]
Every interval in (C6) is divided by \(10^9\).  On the four boxes, respectively, rational interval evaluation of the Jacobian determinants of \((F_1,F_0,S)\) gives
\[
[19,21]10^{12},\quad[10,11]10^{12},\quad[-75,-73]10^{11},\quad[-17,-16]10^{12},
\tag{C7}
\]
so no box contains a multiple or spurious stationary solution.  Direct interval substitution in (C1) and the original tilt formulas gives \(0<z_a<1\), \(0<z_a+d_\vartheta(z_a)<1\), and positive cleared denominators in every box.

The full legal-cell list for \(D_A\) at \(\Gamma_A=16\) is
\[
\begin{split}
&\{(0,0)\},\quad\{(1,1)\},\quad
\{(t,t):0<t<1\},\\
&\mathcal R=\{(W(t),t):0<t<1\},\quad
\mathcal F=\{(1-W(t),1-t):0<t<1\},\\
&\mathcal I_R=\{(w_0,w_1):0<w_1<w_0<1\text{ and both exposure inequalities are strict}\},\\
&\mathcal I_F=\{(w_0,w_1):0<w_0<w_1<1\text{ and both exposure inequalities are strict}\}.
\end{split}
\tag{C8}
\]
On \(\mathcal R\), the common lower and upper branches are \(J_{1/36}\) and \(J_{36}\); on \(\mathcal F\), complementing \(U\) gives the same objective lists with reciprocal tilts.  On the diagonal and both corners the contrast is exactly \(29/100\).  Hence (C5)--(C8) list every boundary, endpoint, and analytic-sign candidate, with the second and first rows of the two respective blocks in (C6) being strictly inferior to the selected lower and upper rows.

For the separate-pair extrema, use the same reverse arc and let \(Q_{1,\vartheta}=53/100+(W-t)d_\vartheta(z_1)/2\) and \(Q_{0,\vartheta}=6/25+(t-W)d_\vartheta(z_0)/2\).  Forming the one-risk analogue of (C2) and eliminating its legal root gives, up to a positive rational factor,
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
Q_{1,1/36}&t^2(t-1)^2(230t-319)(1250t-379)\\
Q_{0,1/36}&t^2(t-1)^2(15t+1)^4(325t-9)(565t-129)\\
Q_{1,36}&t^2(t-1)^2(230t-361)(1250t-421)\\
Q_{0,36}&t^2(t-1)^2(15t+1)^4(2015t+73)(2495t-167).
\end{array}
\tag{C9}
\]
The root \(t=9/325\) in the second row is rejected by the original mixture equation because its stationary solution is \(z_0=414/395>1\); the extra roots in the other rows lie outside \((0,1)\), with stationary solutions \(-636/445\), \(1219/655\), and \(-2/435\), respectively.  The four legal stationary records, including their exact objectives, are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{extremum}&(w_0,w_1)&\vartheta&Q\\ \hline
\min Q_1&(6064/6935,379/1250)&1/36&94711/277400\\
\max Q_0&(516/625,129/565)&1/36&2553/5650\\
\max Q_1&(6736/7565,421/1250)&36&212689/302600\\
\min Q_0&(334/625,167/2495)&36&1797/12475.
\end{array}
\tag{C10}
\]
The arc endpoints, diagonal, and corners give \(Q_1=53/100\) and \(Q_0=6/25\), and complementing \(U\) duplicates (C10).  Equations (C1)--(C10), together with exact rational interval evaluation of the displayed formulas, are the deterministic certificate \(\mathcal C^\star\); no symbolic claim over varying inputs is part of this object.
